0001 | # Four-card consolidation follow-up — October 6 EDT / October 7 UTC
0002 | 
0003 | The owner authorized continuing the consolidation independently. We kept LTX
0004 | and Flash-Next parked, preserved models and experiment history, and raised the
0005 | disk reserve without using the unreliable external drive. No model process,
0006 | GPU test, restart, host power or memory setting change was introduced.
0007 | 
0008 | ## Storage result and recovery
0009 | 
0010 | Eight inactive August runtime/build trees occupied 20,336,185,344 allocated
0011 | bytes (18.94 GiB). Complete tar.zst archives occupy 2,672,559,773 bytes (2.49 GiB)
0012 | under `/home/steve/git-archives/staging-consolidation-20261007/`. Their unpacked
0013 | copies were removed only after verification. This saves about 16.45 GiB net;
0014 | available root space afterward was 57,829,376,000 bytes (53.86 GiB).
0015 | 
0016 | [Audit](../data/maintenance/staging-consolidation-20261007/audit.json),
0017 | [complete verification](../data/maintenance/staging-consolidation-20261007/complete-verification.json),
0018 | and [archive hashes and exact restore commands](../data/maintenance/staging-consolidation-20261007/summary.json)
0019 | preserve the evidence. The immutable sealed q64k32-r2 build remains recoverable
0020 | byte for byte, including source, dependencies, compiled runtime and receipts.
0021 | Historical launchers retain their original path references; restore the
0022 | relevant tree before replaying them. No published runtime pin was replaced.
0023 | 
0024 | The audit found no models, internal symlinks, hardlinked files or special files
0025 | in these trees. Privileged process checks covered command lines, environments,
0026 | maps, open files and working directories, with zero matches or access errors.
0027 | Inbound-link checks were limited to home top-level and tracked repository
0028 | symlinks; they were not a full-system link census.
0029 | 
0030 | Archive creation preserved modes, ACLs and extended attributes. Every archive
0031 | was SHA-256 checked and compared against the original. Independent review
0032 | added complete member inventories to catch files omitted or newly added during
0033 | archival, and directory/receipt fsync before final removal. The complete
0034 | inventories matched the source trees and audit file counts; repeated tar byte
0035 | comparisons passed for all eight trees.
0036 | 
0037 | The initial unprivileged removal hit a write-protected directory in
0038 | `qwen38-gdn-poison-stage-20260822` and stopped. Its complete verified archive
0039 | was restored in place, including the files already removed. All eight sources
0040 | then passed the full inventory and repeated byte comparisons. This also
0041 | rehearsed restoration of that real archived runtime. After a repeated idle-use
0042 | check, privileged removal handled the preserved read-only modes. Archive and
0043 | receipt files plus parent directories were fsynced. Nothing was reconstructed
0044 | from a newer build or silently discarded.
0045 | 
0046 | These archives remain on the internal disk. They protect against accidental
0047 | loss of unpacked staging content, **not failure of that disk**. The external
0048 | EX400U remains unmounted and unqualified after its USB incident.
0049 | 
0050 | The existing storage admission check now admits a planned 3 GiB write while
0051 | retaining 50 GiB, and refuses 5 GiB at this snapshot. Receipts are alongside
0052 | the archive summary. Admission is a point-in-time check, not a reservation;
0053 | budget simultaneous caches, temporary files and outputs before each new job.
0054 | There is no automatic deletion policy or new background service.
0055 | 
0056 | ## Safer future resumption
0057 | 
0058 | - [LTX progress-lock recovery](../experiments/ltx25-b70/recovery/20261007-progress-lock/README.md):
0059 |   the exact installed source leaks its display lock after synthetic ENOSPC.
0060 |   An isolated try/finally patch passes ten CPU tests, preserves error propagation
0061 |   and normal rendering, and is linked from the resume handoff. Nothing is
0062 |   installed or changed in sealed packets. This supports the incident diagnosis
0063 |   but does not prove the original lock owner or GPU correctness.
0064 | - [Qwen TP2 candidate](../experiments/qwen38-27b-b70/release-candidates/20261006-tp2-state-fix/README.md):
0065 |   20 overlay and 14 offline-preflight tests pass. Local vLLM source can ignore an
0066 |   excluded or unimportable plugin, even though registration exceptions propagate.
0067 |   Receipt validation therefore refuses pending/self-declared kernel qualification.
0068 |   No real runtime is allowlisted and no launcher is provided. The exact R314
0069 |   kernel/source evidence and in-process checks in every worker remain required;
0070 |   local older-loader evidence does not qualify R314.
0071 | 
0072 | ## Priorities after consolidation
0073 | 
0074 | 1. Obtain a dependable independent backup destination and copy the preserved
0075 |    research plus archives with read-back verification. Do not regard Git as a
0076 |    backup of model weights or untracked raw experiment artifacts.
0077 |    **Later October 6 update:** [a selected additional EX400U backup](2026-10-06-ex400u-backup-review.md)
0078 |    passed full read-back and restore checks; internal originals remain. This
0079 |    closes the immediate additional-copy gap for its selected scope, while
0080 |    long-term drive reliability and complete-machine coverage remain unqualified.
0081 | 2. Keep the existing RAM exclusion unchanged. **Owner clarification October 6:
0082 |    no RAM replacement in 2026.** Blocks 53–57 were rechecked offline and the boot
0083 |    service enabled. Hardware replacement is removed from the near-term plan;
0084 |    the mitigation remains active and ordinary fault handling still applies.
0085 | 3. Coordinate exact Qwen inputs and owning-host availability, then qualify the
0086 |    candidate with actual kernels, unchanged-model checks and full release
0087 |    evidence. Do not interfere with the other host's active context experiment.
0088 | 4. Resume LTX or Flash-Next when the owner returns to that lane, using its saved
0089 |    handoff and current storage admission. Keep failed trials and original
0090 |    references, and do not silently adopt output-changing performance gains.
0091 | 
0092 | Further deletion is not needed for the immediate unblock. The remaining margin
0093 | is modest; a large new model or build needs separately verified capacity.
END DOCUMENT D01

0001 | # EX400U ordinary-I/O review and additional research backup
0002 | 
0003 | The owner authorized proceeding with backup investigation after confirming that
0004 | RAM replacement is deferred through 2026. Existing memory exclusions remain
0005 | unchanged. This review performs no SMART passthrough, firmware update, filesystem
0006 | repair, driver reset, host restart, power-setting change or GPU workload.
0007 | 
0008 | ## What the incident establishes
0009 | 
0010 | The saved October 6 kernel log first reports a failed vendor command, opcode
0011 | `0xe6`, immediately after the `smartctl -d sntasmedia -a` query. An ordinary read
0012 | later timed out, followed by a kernel-initiated USB reset and read error. This
0013 | supports a passthrough-trigger hypothesis; it does not prove media health or
0014 | establish that the bridge command was the only cause. The SMART report's enormous
0015 | power-cycle/hour counters make its overall health claim unsuitable as a gate.
0016 | 
0017 | The separate August NTFS mirror mismatch remains historical evidence. The
0018 | drive-local health note still calls for Windows filesystem maintenance; this
0019 | review does not establish that it happened. A successful mount is not a full
0020 | filesystem check.
0021 | 
0022 | The saved report identifies firmware ULFM91.0. Corsair documents a disconnect
0023 | problem on some EX400U units with that firmware, but the exposed USB serial does
0024 | not match the advisory's serial format/range, so applicability is unconfirmed.
0025 | The vendor's reinitialization procedure **erases all user data** and requires
0026 | Windows; it was not attempted. [Corsair advisory](https://help.corsair.com/hc/en-us/articles/39222145509137-How-to-Fix-EX400U-Drive-frequently-disconnecting).
0027 | Corsair separately lists ULFM91.2 fixes for a specific USB-port compatibility
0028 | issue and displayed health information. Those notes do not establish that it
0029 | fixes this Linux incident. [Official release notes](https://www.corsair.com/us/en/explorer/release-notes/ssd-firmware/ex400uex400u-survivor-ulfm912/).
0030 | 
0031 | ## Bounded pilot and inward preservation
0032 | 
0033 | Identity: Corsair EX400U, USB `1b1c:1a20`, NTFS partition UUID
0034 | `4E0E66ED0E66CD91`, mounted through `ntfs-3g`. The initial empty mountpoint and
0035 | UUID were checked before a single `ro,norecover` mount. No recovery option or
0036 | force mount was used. Later mounts also used nodev/nosuid/noexec.
0037 | 
0038 | The Flash-Next configuration and index matched independently recorded hashes.
0039 | Beginning/end ranges from two known model shards matched their internal copies,
0040 | 128 MiB total external model data. This is sampled read evidence, not full-model
0041 | verification. No new kernel storage errors appeared.
0042 | 
0043 | Four exact Flash-Next A367/A394 run and supervisor directories existed only on
0044 | the external drive. Their 121 files (14,340,909 bytes) were copied into
0045 | `/home/steve/git-archives/flash-next-rescue-20261007/`, every destination was
0046 | SHA-256 compared with its source, and source files were retained. This preserves
0047 | their current bytes without requalifying historical benchmark correctness.
0048 | 
0049 | After clean unmount, a single `rw,norecover` mount accepted an additive write
0050 | pilot in a new backup directory. A 95,389,557-byte preserved cache archive was
0051 | copied and fsynced. Another clean unmount/read-only remount preceded its complete
0052 | SHA-256 read-back; it matched, and the kernel log remained clean. This justified
0053 | an additional-copy attempt while retaining every internal original.
0054 | 
0055 | ## Backup scope
0056 | 
0057 | Destination: `/mnt/usb-models/lab-backups/steve-b70s-20261007/`.
0058 | The Git bundle and tracked worktree snapshot capture commit
0059 | `8172add663bf29c842129d366ab422df3355b04b`; final review receipts are recorded
0060 | separately. The tracked archive is checked against Git blob identities, avoiding
0061 | incorrect comparison of archive commit timestamps with working-file timestamps.
0062 | 
0063 | The frozen research selection contains 404,095 paths: 348,263 regular files,
0064 | 55,830 directories and two preserved symlinks. Regular-file payload totals
0065 | 65,984,476,250 bytes (61.45 GiB). It includes:
0066 | 
0067 | - the existing consolidation archives, historical Git bundles and inward rescue;
0068 | - mistake/recovery ledgers and the LTX application source;
0069 | - LTX prepared packets, source snapshots, requests, logs and fault evidence;
0070 | - 36 exact reference-output directories and all 2,618 packet-97 output directories;
0071 | - other LTX previews outside the validation tree.
0072 | 
0073 | It excludes model stores, LTX quarantined model copies, other validation outputs,
0074 | the repository's ignored diagnostic models, home credentials and session folders.
0075 | This is not a whole-machine or complete raw-output backup. All omitted and
0076 | included original data remain in place. Symlinks are archived without following
0077 | their targets. Filename screening found no secret-like filenames; this is not
0078 | a content audit of every historical log.
0079 | 
0080 | The NUL path list and selection checksum prevent accidental recursive inclusion
0081 | of unrelated sources or newly created backup files. Source byte comparisons and
0082 | a complete archive-member census are required before accepting the archive.
0083 | Completed files must then survive a clean unmount/read-only remount and full
0084 | SHA-256 read-back. Kernel errors stop new backup I/O; no retries are scheduled.
0085 | 
0086 | ## Completion
0087 | 
0088 | **Completed October 7 at 01:00 UTC; drive cleanly unmounted.** Nine backup files
0089 | total 27,523,871,235 bytes (25.63 GiB), including the compressed research archive,
0090 | Git bundle, tracked snapshot, pilot archive, complete selection and restore/checksum
0091 | controls. All nine SHA-256 hashes matched after clean unmount/read-only remount.
0092 | The research archive passed full source comparison and the complete 404,095-member
0093 | census. The Git snapshot matched all 44,387 tracked blob identities.
0094 | 
0095 | The bundle was restored into a disposable bare repository; its HEAD matched
0096 | the recorded source commit and `git fsck --full` passed. The packet-98 manifest
0097 | and recovered output-size helper were extracted from the external research
0098 | archive into a disposable directory and matched their pre-existing pinned hashes.
0099 | Temporary restore-check directories were removed. Final kernel/mount postflight
0100 | passed, with no new storage/GPU faults. Internal available space was
0101 | 57,758,072,832 bytes (53.79 GiB); all internal originals remain intact.
0102 | 
0103 | One orchestration preflight was invoked while the clean-remount command was
0104 | still finishing. The missing-mount guard refused it before worker launch or
0105 | backup reads. After waiting for that existing command to complete successfully,
0106 | the verification worker ran once. No mount retry or storage-fault recovery was
0107 | performed; [the event receipt](../data/maintenance/backup-review-20261007/readback-preflight-event.json)
0108 | preserves the correction.
0109 | 
0110 | All machine-readable receipts, including [the completion summary](../data/maintenance/backup-review-20261007/summary.json)
0111 | and [full verification](../data/maintenance/backup-review-20261007/verification.json), are under
0112 | [`data/maintenance/backup-review-20261007/`](../data/maintenance/backup-review-20261007/).
0113 | 
0114 | Regardless of verification outcome, the result is an additional copy on a
0115 | different physical drive, not proof of long-term EX400U reliability. Preserve
0116 | the internal sources and keep this drive out of active model/runtime paths.
END DOCUMENT D02

0001 | # LTX resume handoff — October 6, 2026
0002 | 
0003 | The owner paused the four-card LTX lane for consolidation. New experiment
0004 | submissions are stopped and the packet-97 process has exited after **exactly
0005 | one graceful SIGINT**, with no new server started. The process had reached a
0006 | CPU progress-display lock stall after the disk filled. A bounded nonblocking
0007 | Python stack snapshot located the remaining worker in `tqdm` lock acquisition;
0008 | the other pipeline workers were waiting for jobs. Ten seconds of passive DRM
0009 | observations showed no active GPU work before the incident shutdown.
0010 | 
0011 | The [shutdown receipt](../../data/maintenance/consolidation-20261006/ltx-stop.json)
0012 | records `process_gone=true` after the zombie was reaped. Postflight found no
0013 | listener on port 8188, no render-node holders and no kernel GPU faults. No
0014 | hard-kill escalation, restart, reboot or host-setting change was used for this
0015 | shutdown. Do not launch packet 98 until the owner resumes the lane.
0016 | 
0017 | Read [CURRENT.md](../../CURRENT.md) for any later shutdown receipt and live
0018 | host state, and [the stop review](notes/2026-10-06-enospc-stop-review.md) for
0019 | the source-level limits. This is preserved research, not an instruction to
0020 | keep a resident service or launch a campaign. The two-card Qwen lane is separate.
0021 | 
0022 | ## What is accepted, and what is still conditional
0023 | 
0024 | - Accepted reference identity: native distilled BF16 LTX 2.5 at revision
0025 |   `5e6e71018ee1756ed329b697a7b4aedc934dfce9`, 256×256, 25 frames at 24 fps,
0026 |   original two-stage sampling. The owner accepted the short-window encoder
0027 |   on October 4; its fixtures are
0028 |   [`data/stability-01-window-prereg.json`](data/stability-01-window-prereg.json),
0029 |   reference prefix `stability-01-w93c-`. Earlier padded-encoder references
0030 |   remain historical and cannot be compared clip for clip with this baseline.
0031 | - Packet 97 batch 1, two sampler workers, shared pools, second decode worker
0032 |   on card 2: **1.308 seconds per clip, 126/126 exact** against those accepted
0033 |   references. This is the latest completed accepted-reference measurement
0034 |   used here, not the incomplete repeat described below.
0035 | - Batch 2: **0.910 seconds per clip, 613/613 exact**, including proof clips.
0036 |   Batch 4: **0.808 seconds per clip, 611/611 exact**, including proof clips.
0037 |   Both are 600-prompt campaigns checked against their own batch references.
0038 |   Different matrix rounding changes the finished clips versus batch 1.
0039 |   Their adoption still needs the owner's quality decision; neither is silently
0040 |   promoted as lossless against the accepted batch-1 references.
0041 | - The batch-4 stream needed about four clips buffered for continuous playback
0042 |   at its average rate. These are independent clips, not demonstrated
0043 |   clip-to-clip continuation or subsecond request latency.
0044 | 
0045 | Evidence: [packet 97 results](notes/2026-10-06-packet-97-results.md),
0046 | [batch independence and output differences](notes/2026-10-04-packet-96-results.md),
0047 | [accepted window milestone](notes/2026-10-04-milestone-window-baseline.md).
0048 | 
0049 | ## Prepared next experiment
0050 | 
0051 | [Packet 98](notes/2026-10-06-packet-98-build.md) adds a fixed output size per
0052 | server: 256×256, 512×320 or 640×384. It is built and sealed offline and has
0053 | **no GPU throughput or larger-size quality result**.
0054 | 
0055 | Sealed local packet:
0056 | `/mnt/fast-ai/bench-results/ltx25-baseline-20260913/prepared-encoder-size-98`.
0057 | Manifest SHA-256:
0058 | `918b47a5530b4dc97fe8fc8f4ec77fd64521ec6846217c54f5fba589e0e8377f`.
0059 | The builder, runner, CPU checks, memory basis and negative sweep outcomes live
0060 | in this lane; preserve `data/size-98-offline/` in full.
0061 | 
0062 | When the owner resumes LTX, first verify the current host and sealed packet
0063 | identity without changing power or memory settings. Use a fresh health
0064 | admission receipt. The first planned GPU experiment is the packet-98
0065 | **256×256, two-way layout, two workers, batch 1, shared pool, decode replica
0066 | on card 2** control against `w93c`. Only after that control passes should the
0067 | predeclared larger-size plan proceed: first one worker/batch 1 at 640×384,
0068 | then the admitted two-worker/batch-2 case. The build note holds exact commands
0069 | and disjoint output indices; never reuse an existing run directory.
0070 | 
0071 | Larger-size arms are explicitly **speed only**. Their replay and cross-card
0072 | decode checks establish internal consistency, not reference parity or image
0073 | quality. Two-worker/batch-4 at 640×384 is refused by the current memory plan.
0074 | Do not bypass that refusal or convert estimated headroom into a measured claim.
0075 | Baseline adoption and clip-to-clip continuation remain separate decisions.
0076 | 
0077 | ## Consolidation and incomplete-run evidence
0078 | 
0079 | An isolated [progress-lock recovery candidate](recovery/20261007-progress-lock/README.md)
0080 | now reproduces the installed progress bar's ENOSPC lock leak and fixes exception
0081 | cleanup, with ten passing CPU tests. It has not been installed or added to a
0082 | sealed packet. Review it for a successor runtime when resuming; it does not
0083 | repair the incomplete outputs or establish GPU correctness.
0084 | 
0085 | The October 6 disk-full cleanup revealed an empty source helper and an
0086 | unfinished packet-97 repeat. The recovery inventory and guarded CPU test are
0087 | recorded in [`data/consolidation-20261006.json`](data/consolidation-20261006.json).
0088 | 
0089 | - `scripts/ltx_output_size_98.py` was zero bytes. It was recovered from the
0090 |   exact sealed packet file only after verifying both the manifest and its
0091 |   per-file hash. Recovered SHA-256:
0092 |   `895b1c02ac764838b5d69446b0e5cf054884b191dd8b9446c5ce641ec40f2e52`.
0093 | - `data/place-97/two-way-w2-b1-p1-dxpu2-r2/summary.json` was empty and the
0094 |   timed-throughput receipt was absent. Its engine log has 541 complete JSON
0095 |   rows and a truncated final row. Preserve those original bytes; do not
0096 |   invent or promote a summary from the earlier probe. The completed packet-97
0097 |   results above are independent evidence.
0098 | - Three empty legacy CPU sweep logs are retained with their recorded sweep
0099 |   outcomes; an empty log is not a passing test. The broad sweep's historical
0100 |   failures and timeout remain negative evidence.
0101 | 
0102 | For a bounded CPU recheck, run `scripts/test-packet98-size-cpu.py` with the
0103 | baseline virtualenv Python, `-B`, and `scripts/cpu-guard-98.py` installed as
0104 | `sitecustomize.py` in a disposable `/tmp` directory on `PYTHONPATH`.
0105 | Use a 180-second subprocess timeout. The guard prevents accelerator calls,
0106 | endpoint connections, real checkpoint reads and writes outside `/tmp`.
0107 | Capture output to a new log; do not rerun the broad sweep just to repeat
0108 | already-recorded failures. The historical verification driver
0109 | `scripts/verify-review-98-cpu.py --tests` overwrites its prior receipts, so
0110 | preserve those before any deliberate rerun.
0111 | 
0112 | ## Preserve on disk
0113 | 
0114 | Keep the model tree, original tensor/reference archives, all prepared packets,
0115 | the virtualenv and source tree, packet manifests, raw run receipts and fault
0116 | evidence under the linked storage paths. Nothing here authorizes model or
0117 | research-output deletion. Follow the current storage map and verified restore
0118 | receipts before any later archive move.
0119 | 
0120 | Host mitigations are already recorded in `CURRENT.md`: automatic bad-memory
0121 | fencing at boot, kernel 7.0.0-39 and the existing application deferred-backing
0122 | setting. Recent completed packet-97 runs reported no GPU fault or lockup.
0123 | This does not establish permanent hardware repair. Preserve settings and halt
0124 | new requests on a fault; no restart chain, automatic reboot or driver reset.
0125 | 
0126 | For future graceful shutdowns, packet 97's `stop_when_proven` in
0127 | `scripts/run-campaign-97.sh` is the source of the protocol: stop submissions,
0128 | prove an empty queue and completed stage jobs (or stable pipeline idleness),
0129 | recheck the fault latch and exact PID/start identity, send one SIGINT, and
0130 | wait at most 180 seconds without escalating to a hard kill. This is a protocol
0131 | reference, not a command to rerun the campaign or assume a historical PID.

0001 | # Two-card Qwen3.8 27B state-boundary release candidate
0002 | 
0003 | Status: **draft, CPU verified only; GPU qualification and publication pending**.
0004 | No published package, historical overlay, image, launcher or benchmark claim is
0005 | changed by this packet. No model process was launched to prepare it.
0006 | 
0007 | The existing TP2 recipe can read the wrong recurrent-state slot when a highly
0008 | accepted speculative step is followed by a narrower step, including at the end
0009 | of the context window. Research R314 plus the state-width overlay fixes this
0010 | indexing path. This candidate copies that overlay and rejects incompatible
0011 | registration or narrow-step layouts instead of logging an error and continuing
0012 | with the known defective path.
0013 |
